subject: Post-call: procurement path, billing options (PO vs card) & security gating
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@axiomai.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@axiomai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-24T13:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: procurement path, billing options (PO vs card) & security gating

Thanks for carving out time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of the call:
- Use case: real-time summarization + search in AxiomAI support portal (low latency, predictable throughput).
- Expected qps: steady 8-12 requests/s with spikes during incident windows.
- Primary constraint: procurement must confirm billing path (PO or corporate card) and verify SOC 2 / DPA documents before procurement approval.

Key asks from Axiom:
1) Pricing commitment: they asked for monthly committed units vs purely on-demand.
2) Billing path: they prefer PO for orders > $15k/month but are open to card for pilot.
3) Marketplace: possible preference for CloudHub marketplace to simplify procurement and org-level billing.
4) Security: need SOC 2 Type II report, a DPA template, and answers to a short security questionnaire before legal signs off.

Attachments I will send right after this email: SOC2 redacted, DPA draft, and our standard questionnaire.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- Redwood (Rafael): upload redacted SOC2 + DPA draft to shared Drive and send DocuSign link for DPA (today).
- Axiom (Tom): confirm preferred billing path (PO vs card) for pilot and production (by next Tue 2026-05-31).
- Axiom (Samantha): fill basic fields in the security questionnaire and flag any non-standard asks (by 2026-05-28).
- Redwood (Marissa/Karthik): provide procurement contact for marketplace listing and handle any contract redlines (Marissa), and coordinate legal on DPA terms (Karthik).

Immediate asks for you: please confirm whether you want Redwood to route billing through CloudHub marketplace (we can provision a marketplace listing and provide one invoice to your procurement org) or whether your procurement requires a direct PO to Redwood. Also indicate if there are any non-negotiable DPA clauses we should pre-address.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: 2026-05-24T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement path, billing options (PO vs card) & security gating

Thanks Rafael — clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- Pilot: we'll start on a corporate card for the pilot (internal spend cap is $2,500/month).
- Production: procurement wants a PO-based workflow once spend exceeds ~$15k/mo.
- Marketplace: we'd prefer marketplace billing if Redwood is already listed on CloudHub — one invoice to our procurement team simplifies approvals. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a marketplace purchase that gives us org-level invoicing?
- Security: please send SOC 2 redacted and DPA (we need to review). Also Tom will complete the security questionnaire — he may have a few custom asks on retention windows and audit log granularity.

Tom — looping you for procurement specifics.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Product Ops, AxiomAI
Samantha.Lee@axiomai.com

Thanks Rafael — a few procurement-specific clarifications before we can move to legal: 

1) SLA / uptime credits: do you offer month-to-month uptime credits or a financial SLA for Dedicated capacity? We need language we can reference in the PO.
2) Audit logs / access: our security team requires at least 90 days of immutable audit logs for inference requests and must be able to export logs for compliance reviews. Can Redwood provide that?
3) Data residency: we need confirmation that inference never leaves us-east-1 for production traffic (our policy for PII workloads).
4) Marketplace: if we go through CloudHub marketplace, can Redwood accept a marketplace purchase order that maps to our billing center (billing code BIL-1123)?

If you can answer the above, we can route the DPA + PO internally. We're aiming for a decision on billing path and legal approval by next Wednesday (2026-06-02).

Tom Nguyen
Procurement Manager, AxiomAI
Tom.Nguyen@axiomai.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement path, billing options (PO vs card) & security gating

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and next steps: 

1) SLA / uptime credits: For Hosted API we publish an uptime SLO (99.9%) and offer service credits in our enterprise contracts. For Dedicated we can include a specific SLA with financial credits for sustained outages — need Karthik to confirm precise language; we've pushed a standard SLA clause into the DPA draft attached.
2) Audit logs: We retain immutable request/response audit logs for 180 days by default for Dedicated customers; export capability is available via our console and we can provide exports on request for compliance audits. For Hosted API we retain 90 days (can be extended under contract).
3) Data residency: We can pin production workloads to us-east-1 via our Dedicated or Private deployment options; for Hosted API we can route to a US-only region — we'll confirm routing policy with infra and put that in the DPA/Annex.
4) Marketplace purchasing: Redwood supports CloudHub marketplace purchases. We can map marketplace invoices to your billing code BIL-1123 — Marissa will coordinate.

Attached: redacted SOC2 (SOC2_Type2_redacted_2026.pdf) and DPA draft (DPA_Draft_Redwood_v1.docx). I've also attached the questionnaire you requested. If Tom can fill and return the questionnaire, Karthik will triage any legal nuances.

Next items I will do:
- Share DocuSign link for standard DPA (today).
- Email Marissa to start the marketplace onboarding flow and invoice mapping.
- Book a 30-min contract call with Axiom legal + Karthik if there are redlines (proposed window Tue 2026-06-01).

If that sounds good I can open a HubSpot deal note with the mutual action plan and timeline.

Thanks,
Rafael
